reference_sql:
SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_orders
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.store_code
alternatives: SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_orders FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY s.store_code

SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) FILTER (WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00') AS n_orders FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY 1

other_way.sql: SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) FILTER (WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00') AS n_orders FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY 1
other_way.tradeoff: FILTER moves the month test out of WHERE and into the count, which fixes it too, but every order of every month is joined first.
